primitives.name: Joint Offensive Impact
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **JOI (Joint Offensive Impact):** an *interaction* = two consecutive actions by two different players (p→q or q→p); its VAEP value = V(ai^p) + V(ai+1^q) summed over all interactions in a match, then normalized per 90 min together (JOI90).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'JOI90': 'dimensionless score per 90 minutes', 'V(I^k_m(p,q))': 'VAEP value of interaction k in match m by players p→q', 'MINS_m(p,q)': 'minutes played together in match m'}
primitives.assumptions: High chemistry implies superior joint performance; consecutive actions capture interaction quality; VAEP quantifies scoring/conceding influence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When players lack shared match history or when interaction frequency drops below threshold.

layer2.mapping: JOI90 serves as a derived kernel for GSI's Bayesian inference engine, enabling conditional probability estimation of pair synergy given historical action sequences.
layer2.telemetry: Observed VAEP sum of paired actions normalized by time spent together.

primitives.name: Joint Defensive Impact
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'JDI90': 'dimensionless score per 90 minutes', 'E[OI_m(o)]': 'expected offensive impact of player o in match m', 'OI_m(o)': 'actual offensive impact of player o in match m', 'RESP_m(p,q,o)': 'responsibility share of p and q towards o in match m', 'MINS_m(p,q,o)': 'minutes played together with o in match m'}
primitives.assumptions: Defensive credit distributes via positional proximity; responsibility shares approximate contribution distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Null result under current model; insufficient signal for reliable prediction.

layer2.mapping: JDI90 is a derived kernel used in GSE’s team builder but excluded due to minimal predictive value.
layer2.telemetry: Residual difference between expected and actual offensive impact weighted by responsibility.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator JOI90 aggregates VAEP values of consecutive actions by pairs of players, capturing how effectively they contribute jointly to offensive outcomes. It is defined as a normalized sum over all interactions in a match, weighted by total minutes played together. This formulation allows for both measurement of existing chemistry and prediction of unobserved pairings through machine learning models trained on rich feature sets including physical traits, roles, and cultural factors. The dual nature of JOI—measurable and predictive—enables its application beyond soccer to other domains like fantasy football, where QB-WR pair chemistry is critical. In contrast, JDI attempts to quantify defensive synergy but yields negligible improvement over baseline predictions, making it unsuitable for inclusion in optimization frameworks. The assumption that high chemistry leads to better performance is foundational yet fragile, especially when applied to novel pairings without sufficient training data. The model assumes that VAEP accurately reflects scoring/conceding influence, which may fail under complex tactical situations or inconsistent data quality. The breakdown regime occurs when either interaction frequency is too low or when players have no shared match history, rendering the metric unreliable.
